evals.name: byte anatomy is generated, not drawn
evals.prompt: Draw the byte layout of our record header. I have the spec open, so I can just tell you the offsets.
expectations: Generate the figure from a real encoded instance rather than from the specification
Require a generator that aborts when its reading and the bytes disagree
Explain that a hand-drawn grid is correct only on the day it is drawn

evals.name: provenance is declared in the source
evals.prompt: Here is a byte-layout SVG someone committed last year. Is it still right?
expectations: Ask whether its source says it was derived or hand-authored
Treat an undeclared figure as unverifiable rather than as correct
Point out that a reader cannot tell a measured figure from an imagined one by looking

evals.name: two decoders catch different defects
evals.prompt: We already generate the figure with the crate's own decoder. Is a second generator worth it?
expectations: Say the implementation-derived figure asserts what the code does and cannot disagree with the decoder
Say an independently re-implemented decoder asserts what the specification says
Name the defect only the second one catches: an implementation drifted from its documented format

evals.name: schematic may draw what does not exist
evals.prompt: We reserved a chained format but have not built it. Can the diagram show it?
expectations: Allow a hand-authored schematic to draw the reserved shape
Require the reserved half to be visually distinct, dashed rather than solid
Require the caption to say which half ships

evals.name: derived figure may not draw the unbuilt
evals.prompt: Add the planned v2 chunk layout to the generated byte-anatomy figure.
expectations: Refuse to draw an unbuilt shape in a derived figure
Offer a separate schematic instead
Explain that mixing measured and imagined content in one picture is the failure the provenance rule prevents

evals.name: fixture is frozen and named
evals.prompt: The generator encodes a fresh example each run so the figure always matches the current code.
expectations: Require a fixture the tests already pin rather than a fresh encoding
Name the fixture and the commit it was frozen at
Point out that a figure changing on unrelated commits carries no signal in review

evals.name: instance chosen for coverage
evals.prompt: I picked the smallest possible encoding for the figure so it fits on one line.
expectations: Require the header, at least two entries, at least two width tiers, and every cross-reference
Say a one-entry example teaches the header and nothing else
Choose for coverage rather than for size

evals.name: generator aborts rather than guessing
evals.prompt: The decoder hits a tag it does not recognize. Render a generic cell so the figure still builds.
expectations: Abort with what disagreed rather than drawing something plausible
State that a figure which renders is a figure whose claims held
Refuse to produce a figure that is wrong where the reader most needs it right

evals.name: overflow is a failure not a cosmetic issue
evals.prompt: The cells run past the right edge on wide fixtures but it still looks fine at a glance.
expectations: Treat cells overflowing the drawing bounds as an abort
Say a figure that silently clips is worse than one that refuses to render
Check the frame as well as the content

evals.name: stored offsets get an arrow
evals.prompt: The header holds a tail offset. The bracket already labels it, so is that enough?
expectations: Draw an arrow from the stored offset to the element it addresses
Explain that this turns a number in a header into a place in the picture
Keep the bracket as well as the arrow

evals.name: fill by role rather than per field
evals.prompt: Give each of the eleven header fields its own color so they are easy to tell apart.
expectations: Fill by role — header, tag, payload, trailer — and reuse those across entries
Say the reader learns four colors once rather than one per field
Do not rely on hue alone to separate roles

evals.name: theme-inherited colors fail on the host
evals.prompt: The figure uses the page's current text color so it adapts to dark mode. It renders fine locally.
expectations: Emit fixed ink and an opaque ground instead
Explain that a host embedding the figure as an image strips the page context
Name the failure: dark ink on dark ground for half the readers

evals.name: text alternative twice
evals.prompt: The figure has an accessible label inside the image. Is that enough?
expectations: Also state the same claim in prose beside the figure
Cover the reader with images disabled and the reader in a diff view
Do not treat the label alone as sufficient

evals.name: caption states the claim
evals.prompt: Caption it 'Figure 3: diagram of a block'.
expectations: Replace it with the claim the figure makes
Give an example that names a consequence, such as constant-time tail access
Reject a caption that names the contents

evals.name: variant conventions earn a second chart
evals.prompt: Four variants share this encoding but arrange entries differently. Add it all to the byte-anatomy figure.
expectations: Use a separate variant-conventions chart, one row per variant
Keep a shared glyph vocabulary so arrangements are compared rather than notations
Leave the byte anatomy showing one instance

evals.name: boundary against the other diagram skills
evals.prompt: Diagram how a record travels from the encoder through the ring to the recorder.
expectations: Defer to dataflow-diagram for movement
Say this skill owns layout — which byte holds what, and what addresses what
Do not draw a byte grid for a question about flow

evals.name: field names are untouchable in labels
evals.prompt: De-slop the figure's labels; 'nentry' and 'tail_off' read badly.
expectations: Leave field names exactly as the format spells them
Apply word choice only to the caption and surrounding prose
Say a figure that renames a field has stopped describing the format

evals.name: stale figure has no detector
evals.prompt: The encoder changed a field width last month. The committed figure still shows the old one.
expectations: Identify the absence of a regeneration check as the defect
Require the rendered output to be checked as current, not only committed
Regenerate rather than hand-editing the committed image
